subject: Finalizing compensation anchoring & geo-band decision
messages:
From: Mercer Compensation <mercer@consulting.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Global market snapshots v2 (benchmarks attached)

Hi Ava / Laura / Tessa,

Attached is the Q2 market snapshot and percentile mappings for the US, EU, and APAC markets. Key highlights:
- US: tech medians continue to outpace broader market by ~6-8% at L4-L7.
- EU: narrower bands, more compression at senior levels.
- APAC: larger variance across city hubs; Singapore and Sydney align closer to US midpoints.

We included both median and 75th percentile figures and a recommended set of anchoring rules:
1) Use "local-market" anchoring for base salary (city-level when available).
2) Apply role-level uplift factor for critical product/infra roles (5-12%).
3) For distributed hires, use candidate-provided location + capped geo multiplier.

Please review — the .xlsx has the band definitions and the full dataset. If you want, we can prepare a short slide summarizing the options for leadership signoff.

Attachments: market_benchmark_2026_q2.pdf, band_definitions_v2.xlsx

Best,
Mark Ellis
Senior Consultant, Mercer Compensation

From: ava_chen@redwood.com
To: Mercer Compensation <mercer@consulting.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Global market snapshots v2 (benchmarks attached)

Thanks Mark — this looks thorough. A few quick clarifications before I loop in ops and finance:
- On the suggested "local-market" anchoring: does Mercer recommend city-level or state-level for US remote hires when the city is non-metro?
- For the uplift factor: can you provide an example math for L5 SWE in SF vs Austin (numbers from the spreadsheet are fine)?

Internal note: Laura / Tessa — we need to converge on an anchoring rule by Mon 3 Aug to feed the offer ops playbook update. If Mercer can supply the examples above by tomorrow, I'll consolidate and propose one decision path + fallback buckets for leadership.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Director, Talent & People Operations
Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Global market snapshots v2 (benchmarks attached)

Ava / team — quick points from the compensation strategy side:
- I support city-level anchoring for major hubs (SF, NYC, SEA). For Tier-2/U.S. metro and remote we should default to state-level or "primary office" anchor to avoid excessive offer variance.
- Recommend we standardize on percentile targets by band: L3 target 50th, L4-L5 60th, L6+ 65th (with role-critical exceptions).
- Important: any uplift for critical roles must be tied to a headcount approval matrix (we can't give across-the-board increments without approval).

I'll draft a short decision record with the approval flow if folks agree to these anchors.

— Vivek
VP, Talent Strategy

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed band shifts and example math

Hi all — pulling numbers from Mercer's sheet and applying Vivek's percentiles. Example math for L5 SWE:
- SF anchor (median): $175,000 (median). 60th => $186,000.
- Austin anchor (median): $145,000. 60th => $153,000.
- Proposed uplift for infra/serving roles (critical): +8% on top of percentile target. So SF critical L5 => $200,880.

Proposed band definition edits (high level):
- Band ranges by level: use midpoint +/- 12% for L3-L4, +/- 14% for L5-L6, +/- 16% for L7+.
- Geo multipliers: city-tier table (Tier 1: 1.00, Tier 2: 0.88, Remote: 0.82).
- Hiring guardrails: any offer > 15% above midpoint requires VP signoff; >25% requires People + CFO approval.

I've attached the updated band_definitions_v2.xlsx with formulas and a separate sheet "Approval Matrix". Comments inline.

Mina
Head of Total Rewards

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed band shifts and example math

Team — thank you, this is getting to clarity. Two decisions we need to make in leadership:
1) Anchoring rule for non-metro US remote hires (state vs candidate city): I lean state-level default with an override if candidate is located in a documented local market (we'll need a maintained list).
2) Approval thresholds: VP signoff at >12% and People+CFO at >22% would give us a bit more runway for critical hires while controlling cost.

If there's alignment, I propose we convert Mina's spreadsheet into a short decision record and circulate to Exec (Aparna + CFO) for signoff by EOD Wed 5 Aug. Can Mina and Vivek finalize the numbers and I will prepare the cover memo.

Laura
Head of People Operations

From: ava_chen@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 17:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Final decision record draft and next steps — please sign off

Thanks everyone — based on the thread we have an operational decision path:
- Anchoring: Tiered city-anchor for Tier 1 hubs; state-level default for non-metro remote hires; overrides permitted with documented local-market evidence.
- Percentile targets: L3=50th, L4-L5=60th, L6+=65th; critical roles get defined uplift (5-12%) and require headcount & cost approval.
- Approval thresholds: VP signoff at >12% above midpoint; People+CFO signoff at >22%.

Action items:
- Mina: bake Laura's threshold language into band_definitions_v2.xlsx and produce a "decision record" draft (anchoring_decision_record_draft.md). Due: Tue 3 Aug EOD.
- Vivek: create a simple headcount+cost approval flow diagram for the Exec memo. Due: Tue 3 Aug noon.
- Tessa: update offer ops playbook with interim anchors so recruiters have guidance. Due: Wed 4 Aug.

I will circulate to Exec (Aparna, CFO) on Wed for final signoff. If anyone objects to the approach above, raise it now. Otherwise I'll mark this as the working decision and publish once Exec signs.

Attachments referenced: band_definitions_v2.xlsx, anchoring_decision_record_draft.md, market_benchmark_2026_q2.pdf

Best,
Ava Chen
Director, Talent & People Operations
Redwood Inference
